entries.content:
It is difficult to put into words the peculiar torment of that experience. To be at the mercy of another—one who, under the guise of authority, wielded the power to inflict pain—was to be stripped of all dignity and agency. Each time the shock was administered, I felt not only the physical jolt, which was sharp and searing, but a deeper, more corrosive ache within my spirit. There was a sense of betrayal, both by the person who pressed the button and by the authority that sanctioned such cruelty. I found myself wrestling with disbelief: how could another human, perhaps someone I might have trusted under different circumstances, so readily become an instrument of my suffering simply because they were told to do so?

The emotional impact was profound. I felt exposed, vulnerable, and increasingly distrustful—not just of the individual administering the shocks, but of the entire structure that enabled such harm. My mind recoiled from the realization that ordinary people, when pressed by authority, could so easily abandon empathy. There was a growing sense of alienation, a coldness that crept into my thoughts, making me question the very foundations of human decency. Even after the session ended, I found myself haunted by the memory, unable to sleep, my mind brimming with images of pain and helplessness. I fear that this experience has left a mark, a kind of fever in the soul, and I wonder if I shall ever fully recover my trust in others.

metadata.question: Considering your experience as the person receiving the shocks, can you describe how it felt emotionally and physically to be put in a situation where someone else, under authority instruction, was in control of whether you experienced pain?
